summary: m = 2^{e+1} and the 2-part of N₁ is 2^{s+1}; a power of −p that is ≡ 1 there has order divisible by 2^s unless −p ≡ ±1 modulo a large power of 2, which would make p short.

steps.claim: m = 2^{e+1} with s = 22(e+1); and IsServed: χ_K(p) = −1, p not short, o₀ odd, o₀ ≤ 𝔯.
Apply `two_pow_dvd_or_of_pow_eq_one` to −p (prime to N₀ since χ_K(p) ≠ 1) and its order in (ℤ/2^{s+1})^×: either 2^s divides the order, or −p ≡ ±1 modulo a power of 2 controlled by the order.

    (by grind [chiK_eq_one_of_dvd, Fact])).neg_left ▸ mod_cast by simp [← map_pow])
